evidence: Verified structurally against head 3abee5a6add69443e49322e96f9130b834686235 and base 565def869ae50e47e6da7388ea333229050eaf8d; no runtime experiment was needed or run. (a) Present under another name: Q3 does provide explicit daemon-channel mode negotiation, a mode-bound lease, capability-absent fallback and replacement fences. However, its selected negotiation at resume-v090-q3-channel-design.md:24-34 and implementation at src/cli/watch.rs:358-367,399-451 elect V2 solely from daemon capabilities. The CLI WatchRequest at watch.rs:53-56 has only harness/session; neither it nor run_watch/run_session_marked carries support from the stdout consumer. Both base register.js:184 and current register.js:186 spawn the identical watch --harness claude --session SID command. The mechanism therefore negotiates CLI-to-daemon support, not old-JS-to-CLI support. No equivalent consumer election or parser translation was found. (b) Within contract: TRUST-POLICY.md:1524-1528 and task-15-bounded-design-dispositions.md:54,90 explicitly accept complete stdout flush as cooperative FULL OFFER without modappend, transcript or model-uptake proof, and A7 accepts downstream injection loss. That refutes a demand for downstream confirmation, but the finding does not make that demand. It identifies a deterministic incompatibility in this repository's previously shipped parser before any harness injection: base register.js:250 returns immediately for invitation and notice, while the branch adds these kinds only to separately installed register.js:258. No accepted limit explicitly elects this known incompatible installed parser into the new stdout contract. The Q3 CLI selection itself is implemented as specified; the deployment composition is the gap. Accepted render limits at TRUST-POLICY.md:1748-1769 concern oversized ordinary candidates deferred without emission/confirmation and do not apply to successfully emitted, renderable invitation/notice items. (c) Out of scope: this is the existing bundled Claude mod and its documented watch child contract, not a new harness, adversarial consumer, exactly-once guarantee or capacity expansion. The hooks design requires bundled mod route compatibility and Claude mod regressions to remain passing. Setup is separately invoked: src/harness/claude/setup.rs:908-947 calls claude_mod::install, which writes embedded files at claude_mod.rs:591; scripts/install.sh:689-691 explicitly supports skipping setup. Replacing the executable at its installed launch path therefore need not replace the old JS, and the old child's normal restart launches the new executable. Setup/runtime qualification is deferred, not evidence that this mixed installation is safe. (d) Immaterial: it changes presentation outcomes. src/delivery/presentation.rs:107-121 emits invitation/notice kinds; old onLine discards them before received logging or queue insertion, so they cannot reach append or tool context. Nevertheless watch.rs:690-702 flushes the page and sends presentation confirmation; A7's binding notice frontier treats carried notices as offered, and invitation presentation consumes the bounded Watch offer. Canonical history, explicit inspection, receipt timers and acceptance obligations remain, but they do not restore this intended channel presentation. This is significant deployment risk, judged Should-fix rather than loss of canonical messages. (e) Pre-existing: base watch.rs has no V2 presentation loop or capability election; its drain emits message/lazy and attention/attention_cleared, matching the old parser. The base parser's refusal of unknown kinds alone was compatible with the base producer. This change introduces the producer/consumer mismatch. (f) Linter territory: behavioral protocol compatibility, not formatting/style. The finding survives all refutation checks.
